results.use_case: inspect repository file tree and get source code content
results.execution_guidance: IMPORTANT: Follow the recommended plan below. Extract steps before execution, adapt to your current context, execute sequentially with current_step parameter, and check known pitfalls to avoid errors.
recommended_plan_steps: [Required] [Prerequisite]: Confirm repository access and capture default branch/metadata using GITHUB_GET_A_REPOSITORY (baseline ref for later reads).

[Optional (if repository identifier is unknown or GET fails)] [Prerequisite]: Enumerate accessible repositories using GITHUB_LIST_REPOSITORIES_FOR_THE_AUTHENTICATED_USER (select target), then re-run GITHUB_GET_A_REPOSITORY.

[Optional (if you need a stable snapshot across many reads)] [Prerequisite]: List branches using GITHUB_LIST_BRANCHES and resolve branch/tag to a commit SHA using GITHUB_GET_A_REFERENCE (reuse this ref everywhere).
[Required] [Step]: Retrieve the full file inventory using GITHUB_GET_A_TREE (recursive for complete listing; consider non-recursive first if extremely large).
[Required] [Step]: Verify inventory completeness using GITHUB_GET_A_TREE (proceed only if data.truncated==false).
[Optional (if the tree payload is too large to inspect)] [Step]: Summarize/sanity-check paths using COMPOSIO_REMOTE_WORKBENCH (top-level entries, extension counts).
[Required] [Next Step]: Browse directories or read files using GITHUB_GET_REPOSITORY_CONTENT (keep ref/SHA separate from path; if 404, list parent to confirm casing; dir returns list vs file object).

[Optional (if you need raw bytes or don’t want Base64 decoding)] [Next Step]: Retrieve content using GITHUB_GET_RAW_REPOSITORY_CONTENT (consume any returned download pointer immediately if bytes aren’t inline).
[Fallback (if data.truncated==true or key paths are unclear)] [Fallback]: Discover candidate paths using GITHUB_SEARCH_CODE_ALL_PAGES, then confirm exact locations via GITHUB_GET_REPOSITORY_CONTENT.
known_pitfalls: [GITHUB_GET_A_TREE] Large recursive trees can look cut off in client previews even when complete—trust data.truncated and parse the full payload.
[GITHUB_GET_A_TREE] data.tree[].type differentiates directories ("tree") vs files ("blob"); treating all paths as files breaks follow-on reads.
[GITHUB_GET_REPOSITORY_CONTENT] Directory reads return a list while file reads return an object with base64 content—strip whitespace and fix padding to avoid "Incorrect padding".
[GITHUB_GET_RAW_REPOSITORY_CONTENT] May return a temporary download pointer rather than inline bytes; consumers must fetch/consume via that pointer promptly.
[COMPOSIO_REMOTE_WORKBENCH] Request schema is strict; the executable field name must be code_to_execute or validation can fail.

reference_workbench_snippets.description: Summarize a large GITHUB_GET_A_TREE response (top-level entries + extension counts) from JSON on stdin.
reference_workbench_snippets.code:
```python
import sys,json
from collections import Counter
j=json.load(sys.stdin)
t=j["results"][0]["response"]["data"]["tree"]
top=set();ext=Counter()
for it in t:
 p=it.get("path","")
 if p and "/" not in p: top.add((it.get("type"),p))
 if it.get("type")=="blob":
  n=p.rsplit("/",1)[-1]
  if "." in n: ext[n.rsplit(".",1)[-1].lower()]+=1
print(sorted(top));print(ext.most_common(20))
```

reference_workbench_snippets.description: Decode Base64 text from a GITHUB_GET_REPOSITORY_CONTENT response JSON on stdin (handles whitespace/padding).
reference_workbench_snippets.code:
```python
import sys,json,base64,re
j=json.load(sys.stdin)
d=j.get("content") or j
s=re.sub(r"\s+","",d.get("content",""))
s+="="*((-len(s))%4)
sys.stdout.write(base64.b64decode(s).decode("utf-8","replace"))
```

GITHUB_GET_A_REPOSITORY.description: Retrieves detailed information about an existing and accessible GitHub repository.

repo.description: The name of the repository, without the `.git` extension. This field is case-insensitive.

owner.description: The username of the account that owns the repository. This field is case-insensitive.

GITHUB_GET_A_TREE.description: Browse and list all files/directories in a GitHub repository. Efficiently retrieves the complete repository structure in a single API call when used with recursive mode. Perfect for analyzing codebase structure, finding specific files, or getting an overview of repository contents without cloning.

repo.description: Repository name without owner or .git extension (e.g., for github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes, repo is 'kubernetes').

owner.description: Repository owner username or organization name (e.g., for github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes, owner is 'kubernetes').

tree_sha.description: Branch name (e.g., 'main', 'master'), tag name (e.g., 'v1.0.0'), commit SHA, or tree SHA. Directory paths are NOT supported - use a branch/tag to get the full tree, then extract the directory's SHA from results.

recursive.description: Set to True (or '1'/'true') to fetch the ENTIRE repository file tree recursively (all files and directories in one call). Set to False or leave empty to fetch only the top-level files/folders. For browsing or analyzing the full repository structure, use recursive=True.

GITHUB_GET_REPOSITORY_CONTENT.description: Retrieves a file's Base64 encoded content or lists a directory's contents from a GitHub repository.

ref.description: The name of the commit, branch, or tag to read from. Use this parameter to specify which branch (e.g., 'feat/godlocal-dev', 'main', 'develop'), tag (e.g., 'v1.2.0'), or commit SHA you want to access. If not provided, the repository's default branch will be used. Note: Branch names should be passed here, NOT in the path parameter.

path.description: Required. Path to file or directory in the repository. Empty string ('') retrieves root directory contents. Leading slashes auto-stripped. CRITICAL: Do NOT pass branch names here (e.g., 'feat/godlocal-dev', 'main'). Branch names belong in the `ref` parameter. Path should be file/directory path only (e.g., 'src/main.js', 'README.md'), NOT prefixed with branch name (use 'src/main.js' not 'main/src/main.js'). File paths must include extension (e.g., 'README.md', not 'README'). For common files (README, LICENSE, CHANGELOG) without extensions, action auto-tries common extensions (.md, .txt, .rst). Paths are case-sensitive. On 404 errors, list parent directory to verify exact path/casing.

repo.description: Required. The name of the repository, without the `.git` extension. This name is not case sensitive.

owner.description: Required. The account owner of the repository. This name is not case sensitive. Can also accept full repository path in format 'owner/repo' - the repo part will be extracted automatically.

GITHUB_LIST_BRANCHES.description: List branches in a GitHub repository. Returns branch names, commit information, and protection status. Use this action when you need to retrieve all branches in a repository, optionally filtered by protection status. This is useful for identifying available branches, checking which branches are protected, or preparing to create pull requests.

page.description: The page number of the results to fetch. For more information, see 'Using pagination in the REST API'.

repo.description: The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.

owner.description: The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.

per_page.description: The number of results per page (max 100). For more information, see 'Using pagination in the REST API'.

protected.description: Setting to `true` returns only branches protected by branch protections or rulesets. When set to `false`, only unprotected branches are returned. Omitting this parameter returns all branches.
